case_name: Pasupuleti Siva Ramakrishna Rao v State of Andhra Pradesh and others
facts: The victim P.W.1 (Pasupuleti Siva Ramakrishna Rao) was the President of Bhimavaram Taluk Lorry Workers Union.
A-1 - Chintha Srinivasa Rao @ Bandi Srinu and A-2 - Chintha Krishna @ Bandi are brothers.

About a fortnight prior to the date of incident - 20.04.1998, the victim P.W.1 (Pasupuleti Siva Ramakrishna Rao) and some other Lorry Workers collected Rs.10,000/- as donations to perform the marriage of the daughter of a poor lorry worker.

On 20.04.1998 at about 8.00 pm when P.W.1 (Pasupuleti Siva Ramakrishna Rao) was in the Lorry Workers Union Office near Anakoderu Canal in Undi Road, Bhimavaram, the accused armed with deadly weapons entered the office, abused P.W.1 (Pasupuleti Siva Ramakrishna Rao) in filthy language and threatened him with death because he had collected donations from their area.
They attacked him. A-1 - Chintha Srinivasa Rao hit him on his head with a cool drink bottle causing a grievous injury and instigated other accused to tie a telephone wire around his neck to kill him.
issues: Whether the High Court correctly modified the conviction u/s.307 IPC read with S.34 IPC to S.324 IPC?

Whether the incident occurred when P.W.1 (Pasupuleti Siva Ramakrishna Rao) was in the Lorry Workers Union Office and not at any private place, hence ipso facto set aside the conviction and sentence u/s.452 IPC read with S.34 IPC?
petitioner_arguments: The prosecution need not prove the overt act of the accused.

As regards charge under S.34 IPC, the Trial Court relied on the settled position in law that it is not necessary that there should be a clear positive evidence about the meeting of mind before the occurrence and that if there are more than one accused a common intention to kill can be inferred from the circumstances of the case.
respondent_arguments: The High Court observed that the injuries were not only simple but were trivial.

As regards Injury No.5, it observed that though the Medical Officer stated that the injury was dangerous to life, it is not clear as to how the witness stated so, meaning thereby that there was no explanation for the medical opinion.
court_reasoning: The Trial Court correctly appreciated the evidence and rejected the argument that the other witnesses were not reliable because they were interested witnesses.

As regards charge u/s.452 IPC, the Trial Court held that there was clear intention of accused here and that it was clearly established that the accused went to the office of P.W.1 (Pasupuleti Siva Ramakrishna Rao) in a car and the other circumstances clearly establish that there was preparation for committing the offence.
holding: The High Court modified the conviction u/s.307 IPC read with S.34 IPC to S.324 IPC.

The incident occurred when P.W.1 (Pasupuleti Siva Ramakrishna Rao) was in the Lorry Workers Union Office and not at any private place, hence ipso facto set aside the conviction and sentence u/s.452 IPC read with S.34 IPC.
cases_cited: Pasupuleti Siva Ramakrishna Rao v State of Andhra Pradesh
